angle: DL/EDGE: pass-rush-drill get-off burst and Run-the-Hoop bend (Hoop G), year-standardized, against NFL get-off (NGS season), NFL first-second burst, NFL bend and career pressure rate; baseline = log pick + weight + EDGE share + NGS athleticism + official 10-yd split + 3-cone, leave-one-class-out; decision use = day-3 tiebreaker when no-tracking forecasts are within 0.5 pressure-rate points
metric_name: Hoop G: hardest 0.5 s of sideways (centripetal) acceleration on the Run-the-Hoop lap, g, z within Combine year (contrast: rush-drill burst, yards in the first second of the pass-rush drill)
headline_number: Out of class (n=77, slope of held-out miss on the drill): Hoop G +1.8 pressures per 450-rush season per sd [0.2, 3.4], within-class shuffle p=0.02, 33% above the 2.25 action margin, positive in 2023 and 2024 and flat in 2025; burst -0.5 [-2.3, 1.3], 1% above margin, TOST p=0.06. Day-3 ties (125 pairs, 47 rushers, forecasts within 0.5 pts): higher Hoop G picks the better NFL rusher 56% [43, 69], p=0.20; net +2.6 pressures per decision [0.1, 5.1], p=0.03; worst-case expected cost if Hoop G is noise 0.4. Earlier pick 50%, NGS score 47%.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of the DL Hoop G lineage (round 17 cand_1, 7.55, which lost on missing figures), applying the round-17 winner's transferable top_changes. (1) One headline estimand scored only out of class (slope of the held-out residual on the drill, in pressures per season), with interval (class-stratified player bootstrap that refits every fold) and p (within-class permutation) computed for that estimand, so they agree. The training-fold slope 0.55 is no longer quoted. (2) TOST equivalence for burst against the pre-set margin (p=0.06), and the bootstrap probability of clearing the margin for Hoop G (33%). (3) The decision is now a decision-grade tie rule: tie = no-tracking forecasts within the 0.5-pt margin. The text explains why a pick-gap threshold fails here (median pick gap in ties 54, earlier pick right 50%). Win rate and pressures gained are reported against four tracking-free tiebreakers, with the cost of being wrong (worst case 0.4 pressures per decision) and an effective n of 47 rushers rather than 125 pairs, using player-clustered inference. (4) Go now requires being at least 0.5 pts above the forecast, so the Go calls are only Sawyer and Brinson; Biggers moves to Hold. Each call has a 2026 flip rate and a decision date. (5) Added verify.py, which recomputes Table 1, both held-out slopes, the forecasts and the tie results from inputs.csv (columns documented in inputs_schema.json) in under a second and diffs them against numbers.json. Full analysis runs in about 3 minutes. (6) Added the 40-clip laser-offset caveat. Cut the snap figure, the film-check table and the appendix machinery. The lede uses one unit, pressures per season. 4 figures + 2 tables, 1,923 words; all figures regenerated by the script and visually checked.
open_risks: Tie-rule hit rate is unproven (56%, p=0.20); the significant net gain (p=0.03) rests on a few large differences, so judges may see the same win-rate vs size tension they flagged for the receiver tiebreaker

Hoop G was selected after earlier rounds screened drill measures on these same classes, and the tie analysis was built this round on the same data; 2026 is the first clean test (power 43% for one class)
The out-of-class effect is flat in the 2025 class (-0.02 pts per sd), the class whose players are named in the calls
No-tracking baseline overfits (held-out R2 -0.02 vs 0.10 for pick+role); the R2 gain for Hoop G includes zero (0.06 [-0.20, 0.25])
Hoop G reliability rests on 10 linemen with two laps (0.37); NFL bend has no blockers and may be an effect of winning
3-cone did better than Hoop G in ties (77%) but on only 13 pairs; the rule tells clubs to use the 3-cone first, which narrows Hoop G's role
